title: Red Norvo after Sauter left
summary: Glenn Miller's rise, Red and Harry James at the Ben Franklin, Red's later trio with Tal Farlow.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Red made a lot of fads at the right time, but at the same period I was leaving Red, Glenn Miller had just begun (inaudible), so he walked off with it that year.
I think it was a year later I went to the Ben Franklin in Philadelphia with Red and he followed Harry James or
Harry James followed Red, I forgot now. Harry James took off and left Red there, because Red was always too good. That was always his problem, he liked music.
Harry was a good looking guy and a good player (inaudible).
It might have been Red's instrument; I doubt it though. At that time he was still playing xylophone, maybe tha's what caused him to switch to vibraphone; I don't know. But Red's still there.

You bet he is. I wonder if he regrets it; I really don't know. I know that shortly after that he gave up all ideas of having a band of his own, and a big one. He went to work for Woody, he spent a couple of years on the beach.
He had some marvelous small groups, the trio he had with
That was a wonderful group. Tal Farlow was another story. I see in the paper he just came to New York again.
He did a concert with Tommy Flanagan and Red Mitchell down in the Village. He's sort of a semi recluse. He stays down at the Jersey shore.
Basie too is from Red Bank; that's right there.
